summary: Ravi (synthetic), 40 months, was seen by Demo Therapist after a parent intake call. The therapist confirmed poor eye contact, no response to his name in three attempts, hand flapping during play and solitary play with lining up of toys. The mother reports that Ravi said a few words at age 2 and then stopped talking, that he repeats lines from cartoons, does not point, covers his ears at kitchen sounds, has big tantrums when the route to school changes and hits his own head when upset. The family history includes a maternal uncle who started talking late. This summary documents observations and parent reports; it is not a diagnosis.
reason_for_referral: Reported loss of early words after age 2 and head hitting when upset, together with confirmed social communication differences, need specialist review.
questions_for_specialist: Is further assessment of the reported loss of words recommended?
Are hearing and medical checks needed before the next steps?
What support do you advise for the head hitting at home?
Which follow-up should the therapy team plan with the family?
